brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.evidence: Seven full hex bases placed at a centre cell (0,0) and its six neighbours (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,-1), (0,1), (1,-1), (1,0), all on level 0; the build's piece count is 7.
Seven full top covers added, one on each base (cover:...;full;top), so the top of the honeycomb is closed.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added 18 solid end caps on every open outside face of the perimeter; lockJoints added 12 joint bolts. check_build reports no issues and meshClash 'clear'.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell flower of full hex bases (centre plus six surrounding), with a full top cover on each cell, 18 end caps on the open perimeter faces, and joints locked. check_build is clean with meshClash clear. I did not add props, since the brief is about structure only.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
